or follow requester/policy_manager.cpp:159
```cpp
auto PolicyManager::marshal_config() -> nlohmann::json
{
    return nlohmann::json{
        {POLICY_VERSION_ID, POLICY_VERSION},
        {Policy::enabled_t::name, enabled_},
        {Policy::secure_session_enabled_t::name, secure_session_enabled_},
        {Policy::verify_certificate_t::name, verify_certificate_},
        {Policy::allow_extended_algorithms_t::name, allow_extended_algorithms_},
        {Policy::allowed_versions_t::name, to_json(allowed_versions_)},
        {Policy::allowed_algorithms_aead_t::name,
         to_json(allowed_algorithms_aead_)},
        {Policy::allowed_algorithms_base_hash_t::name,
         to_json(allowed_algorithms_base_hash_)},
        {Policy::allowed_algorithms_base_asym_t::name,
         to_json(allowed_algorithms_base_asym_)},
    };
}
```
Done

I am thinking we should have default policy in spdm repo which serves as a reference, then each BMC can decide what to allow in their platform and modify accordingly.

@ratankgupta31@gmail.com any thoughts on this?

> I am thinking we should have default policy in spdm repo which serves as a reference, then each BMC can decide what to allow in their platform and modify accordingly.

> 

I disagree, The default values for the policies are already debated and documented in PDI. if you need changes for the defaults please create a new comment and we can discuss the rationale for that over there.I dont think we should be halting this review because of that.

Default values in PDI are false in all the cases, like SPDM enabled, Secure session enabled. Some BMCs will have use case not to support secure session and some BMCs not, that policy needs to be determined at compile time for the platform.
This patch expects policy.json in /lib/spdm, for someone enabling for their platform there is no reference json. If we can have example.json with default values(same as PDI) i think it simplifies the integration.

This commit is not meant for adding any configuration file, it is meant to only add infrastructure that persists the existing dbus settings. If you need  configuration file, please open a new commit adding that functionality.

>  Some BMCs will have use case not to support secure session and some

Current Dbus interface default value for SPDM communication is set to false 

name: Enabled
    type: boolean
    default: false
    description: >
        Indicates whether SPDM communication is enabled.

Requiring system administrators to use the Redfish API to enable SPDM communication or verify certificate on every SPDM-capable system is not a scalable approach.

IMHO, the default value for SPDM communication should be set to true.
